questions.question_html:
Identify the correct statements from the following
(I) SnCl2 is ionic, but SnCl4 is covalent in nature
(II) All linear diatomic molecules have zero dipole moment
(III) Both NO and O2 are paramagnetic

questions.option_b: (I) and (III) only
questions.option_c: (II) and (III) only
questions.option_d: (I), (II) and (III)
questions.solution_html:
Among the given statements only I and III are correct and II is incorrect.
All linear diatomic molecules does not have zero dipole moment. e.g. HF, HCl,HBr etc. Hence, statement II is incorrect.
According to Fajan's rule the central metal with more oxidation state will be considered to be more covalent molecule than that have low oxidation state. In SnCl2 and SnCl4 the oxidation state of Sn is +2 and +4 respectively.
Thus, SnCl4 is more covalent.
Due to the presence of one unpaired electron in NO and two in O2, both are paramagnetic in nature.

Assertion (A) :- Adsorption is an exothermic process
Reason (R): - Physisorption of a gas on a solid surface is normally reversible
questions.option_a: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of <fmath alttext="(A)" class="fm-inline"><mrow><mo class="fm-mo-Luc">(</mo><mi class="fm-mi-length-1" mathvariant="italic">A</mi><mo class="fm-mo-Luc">)</mo></mrow></fmath>

Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion. The correct reason for given assertion is as follows : When a gas is adsorbed on a solid surface, its movement is restricted. This leads to a decrease in the entropy of the gas i.e. ∆ S. is negative. Now, for a process to be spontaneous, ∆G should be negative.
We know that, ∆G=∆HH−T∆S
Now, ∆S is negative, ∆H has to be negative to make ∆G negative. Hence, adsorption is always exothermic.
